FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Part 3 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Artificial Limbs, Rehabilitation Appliances and Equipment for the Disabled 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Division 
Council. 

This standard ( Part 3 ) is one of the series establishing a vocabulary of terms used in the field of 
external limb prosthetics and external orthotics. It defines term relating to external orthoses that 
encompass joints. The other parts in this series are: 

Part 1 General terms for external limb prostheses and external orthoses, and 

Part 2 Terms relating to external limb prostheses and wearers of these prostheses. 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from ISO 8549-3 : 1989 
'Prosthetics and orthotics — Vocabulary — Part 3 : Terms relating to external orthoses', issued by 
the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ). 



IS 13970 (Part 3): 1994 

Indian Standard

2,19 Thoraco-Lumbo-Sacral Orthosis ( TLSO ) 2.27 Caliper 



'Orthosis^ that encompasses the whole or a part 
of the *thoracic, the Numbar' and the 'sacro-iliac 
regions' of the *trunk\ 

2.20 Cervical Orthosis ( CO ) 

'Orthosis' that encompasses the whole or a part 
or the *cervical region', including the atlanto- 
occipital joint. 

2.2i Cervlco-Thoracic Orthosis ( CTO ) 

'Orthosis' that encompasses the whole or a part 
of the 'cervical' and the 'thoracic regions', 
including the atlanto-occipital joint. 



2.22 CerWco-Thoraco-Lumbo-Sacral 
( CTLSO ) 



Ortliosis 



'Orthosis' for the Mower limb' which may be used 
permanently or for a short period of time. Its 
functions are: 

a) to provide stability for a weakened^ 
paralysed or unstable limb, 

b) to relieve weight bearing, 

c) to relieve pain, 

d) to control deformity aggravated by postural 
forces, and 

e) to restrict the movement of the joints of the 
Mower limb'. 

3 ALPHABETICAL LIST OF ABBREVIATIONS 



'Orthosis' that encompasses the whole or a part 
of the 'cervical', the 'thoracic', the 'lumbar' and 
the 'sacro-iliac regions', including the atlanto- 
occipital joint. 

2.23 Corset 

An encircling garment with stiffening reinforce- 
ment that attempts to contain soft tissue under 
pressure at a desired elevation^ to compress bony 
and other tissues to restrict or prevent motion or 
to support the muscles and other soft tissues, 

2.24 Brace 

Orthotic device used to hold the part of limb/ 
body in desired position to give support. 

2.25 Splint 

Rigid or flexible appliance used for prevention of 
movement of a joint or for the fixation of displac- 
ed or movable parts. 

2.26 Artiflcial Limb 

Device which works mechanically by muscle 
power, or hydraulically, or by means of electrical 
stimulation. It is made on scientific basis and 
the information given by a surgeon to fulfill the 
essential requirements of a patient whose limb is 
amputcd because of trauma or disease or is 
absent congenitally to a maximum possible of 
function. It is usually made of plastics, wood, 
leather, aluminium, etc.
